katlctl: move trusted-network clusters to mTLS with enable-mtls (#696)

* katlctl: move trusted-network clusters to mTLS with enable-mtls

Add `katlctl management enable-mtls`, which moves an installed
trusted-network cluster to mTLS management without reprovisioning. It
checks every node over plaintext first (reachable, same installation,
new enough, idle, healthy, clock within the certificate backdate),
creates or reuses the secrets file before touching a node, then moves
the nodes one at a time in config order through the node's
confirm-or-revert trial: begin, reach the node over mTLS, confirm,
check plaintext is refused, and wait for health. Only after every node
is confirmed does it write managementAuthentication and
managementIdentity into the ClusterConfig and refresh a saved context.
State is derived from the config, the secrets file and each node's
reported management mode, so a rerun resumes an interrupted or reverted
node and a finished cluster reports that it already uses mTLS.

NodeStatus.management now reports the node clock for the preflight
clock check, and node status and cluster status show each node's
management mode and any trial or revert.

Release-Note: katlctl: move a trusted-network cluster to mTLS management in place with `katlctl management enable-mtls`

* katlctl: address enable-mtls review findings

Refuse a --trial-window outside the node's bounds, using the bounds
nodeidentity now exports, or one that is not whole seconds, before
preflight. Report an interrupt during Begin as interrupted, since
the trial may have started. Start from an mtls config without a
secrets file when every node still answers plaintext trusted-network
management. Make the hint about other secrets depend on the mode,
and tell an operator resuming an expired trial that has not reverted
yet to wait for the revert.

Root cause of the ignored Ctrl-C: run() executed the root command
without a context, so commands that read cmd.Context() got cobra's
background context instead of the interrupt context. The root command
now carries it.

transport.PlaintextAtTLS is now the one plaintext-at-TLS classifier. The
enable-mtls VM scenario gets a lane of its own so the cluster lane
stays clear of its 75m timeout.

Release-Note: skip

* katlctl: show an interrupted enable-mtls trial in status

While an enable-mtls trial is live, the node refuses plaintext, but the
operator's ClusterConfig stays trusted-network until every node is
confirmed. node status and cluster status then printed only the generic
"likely serves mTLS" error, with no trial, deadline or resume step.

When a trusted-network status read meets a TLS listener and the
enable-mtls secrets for this config exist, status now reads the node
over mTLS with them and shows the trial row, its deadline and the rerun
command. Without the secrets, the error says the node may be on an
interrupted trial and how to resume it. Mutating commands keep their
configured credentials.

Closes #708

Release-Note: skip

* katlctl: point mode guidance at enable-mtls

enable-mtls moves a trusted-network cluster to mTLS in place, but
config init, the plaintext-endpoint error, the missing-mode error and
the docs still said that changing the mode requires reprovisioning.
They now name enable-mtls for trusted-network to mTLS, and say that
mTLS to trusted-network is unsupported in place.

The final health poll in enable-mtls could exhaust the deadline and
replace an already observed diagnosis, such as the API proxy still
starting, with a bare deadline error. It now keeps the earlier
diagnosis, which also removes the flake in
TestEnableMTLSChecksAPIProxyAfterConfirm.

Release-Note: skip

* vmtest: use the exported world SSH key helper in enable-mtls

Main moved the world SSH key helper into the vmtest package as
EnsureWorldSSHKey, so the enable-mtls scenario no longer compiled after
rebasing onto it.

Release-Note: skip

* katlctl: never fall back to plaintext after a TLS failure

enable-mtls fell back to plaintext after any failed mTLS status call,
including a certificate verification failure, and could then send the
transition and the node's server key over an unauthenticated
connection. It now takes the plaintext path only when the TLS
handshake received a plaintext HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame; any other TLS
failure stops with a verification error.

A rerun now verifies on every node that plaintext management is
refused, and runs the health gate, before it publishes the mTLS config
or reports success, including when no node remains to migrate. It
repairs a stale saved context or prints the exact context save
command. Interrupted Begin and confirmation calls report the trial
deadline and whether the node may already be committed, deadlines are
shown corrected for node clock skew, a node without node_time falls
back to the workstation clock, resume guidance keeps a custom --output
path, and upgrade guidance names katlctl node upgrade.

Release-Note: skip

* katlctl: classify the management transport from wire evidence

The plaintext decision in enable-mtls still matched a marker in gRPC
error text, which a peer can influence, so a plaintext-capable endpoint
could still receive the transition and server key. The transport
package now observes the first frame the endpoint returns to a TLS
handshake and classifies it as TLS, plaintext HTTP/2 or unknown;
enable-mtls takes the plaintext path only on a complete SETTINGS frame
on stream 0, and stops before starting a trial when the transport
cannot be classified.

A rerun takes its health requirements from the node's installed
Kubernetes role and the cluster configuration rather than from its
current state, so a node degraded after confirmation blocks
publication. The confirm-or-revert trial has not shipped, so an agent
that omits node_time is refused with upgrade guidance, and status shows
a trial deadline only when corrected by the observed node time.

Release-Note: skip

* nix: update the Go module hash for x/net/http2

The transport package now imports golang.org/x/net/http2 directly to
classify the management transport, which changes the vendored module
set and so katlctl's vendorHash; go mod tidy also marks x/net as a
direct dependency.

Release-Note: skip

* katlctl: hold enable-mtls to valid SETTINGS and the installed VIP

Classify a peer as plaintext HTTP/2 only when its initial SETTINGS
are valid for a server, including a disabled push and an in-range
priority setting. Keep an installed control-plane VIP required after
confirmation even when the input configuration omits its advertisement,
and make the migration test inject the legacy marker where enable-mtls
actually reads it.

Release-Note: skip

* katlctl: keep requiring a released Katl-owned VIP on retry

Decide whether enable-mtls must restore a VIP from the agent's installed
endpoint status rather than from its current readiness. A retry after
confirmation released the VIP therefore still refuses to publish,
while a VIP whose ownership Katl does not manage remains eligible
for migration.

Release-Note: skip
